hypothesis: The first restore wave after a long publish phase stalls because of the client, not Lambda. bench.py at the pinned baseline reuses one boto3 Lambda client, so its pooled keep-alive HTTPS connections idle through the publish phase and silently go dead. An invoke written into one never reaches Lambda and ends in a client read timeout. Alternatives to rule out: (a) the version's age since publish; (b) SnapStart cache warm-up for a version never invoked before.

changed_variable.name: lambda_invoke_client_lifetime
changed_variable.baseline: one client for lifecycle calls and every invoke (bench.py at aac59d4)
changed_variable.experiment: a new client per invocation wave, lifecycle calls on a separate retrying client

conditions.client_host: ip-10-0-3-99 (ap-southeast-2 private subnet, NAT egress), python 3.14.6, boto3 1.43.93

conclusion: INVESTIGATION: CAUSE FOUND. The status is 'failed' only because this run has no model-latency phases by design (a 128 MB sleep function); it is not a failed investigation. The first-restore-wave stall is client-side. With one reused client, a measured wave after 400, 700 or 1100 s of pool idle got 1/10 (reuse_poll, the aac59d4 bench.py shape, where the survivor rode the connection kept alive by readiness polls) or 0/10 (reuse_nopoll). The rest ended in client:ReadTimeoutError at 120 s. After 30 (actually 52) or 200 s of idle, every invoke succeeded (10/10). A fresh client succeeded 100/100 at every idle length, both on a never-invoked v2 that was 0 to 1048 s old and on an old v1 idle for up to 1102 s. That rules out (a) the version's age and (b) SnapStart cache warm-up. Lambda-side Invocations and START lines equal the client ok count in every cell, so the stalled requests never reached Lambda. Each stalled socket stayed ESTABLISHED with about 1,785 B unacknowledged and retransmits climbing from 2 to 7; urllib3's dropped-connection check returned false. The threshold lies between 200 and 400 s on this host's NAT egress path. The element that drops the flow was not identified: no RST was seen, although AWS documents one for NAT gateway idle timeout. Fix on lkai/df45-restore-stall: bench.py gives every wave a new invoke client (P1's later e262455 has the same shape). Affected published data: P3 20261020T124451Z lost 45 restore rows and has 45 warm-labelled restores, all excluded by summarize.py. Its affected restore arms retain n=23 (rep) and n=32 (telemetry); unaffected arms retain n=50. Only sample counts shrink; accepted latency rows are not mixed with the dropped or misclassified rows. E1's first attempt was discarded. No published restore latency needs correction. Limitations: one host, one path, one run; the threshold was not bisected; TCP keepalive was not tested. Full write-up: examples/lambda-kleidiai/baseline/restore_stall/README.md on the branch.
